clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 74%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bills offense ranks 1st, the Cardinals defense ranks 27th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 2-1 over their last three games; ARI are 1-2. They also have about 9 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, BUF are at home.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 3.5% of dropbacks (1st), and the Cardinals get home on 5.6% (27th).
The Bills score 26.6 points a game (6th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 26.8 (31st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: The Cardinals score 19.4 points a game (24th in the league), and the Bills allow 18.7 (3rd).
The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 6.8% of dropbacks (22nd), and the Bills get home on 7.5% (8th).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: ARI's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but ARI have pressured the quarterback on 12% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Allen and stalls drives.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 74% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 74 of them. That means the Cardinals win 26, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Bills by 6.5, about 73%. I'm at 74%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

body: The Panthers score 13.9 points a game (31st in the league), and the Saints allow 19.2 (6th).

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Dolphins at 61%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Dolphins offense ranks 2nd, the Jaguars defense ranks 24th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Hard Rock Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Dolphins gain 6.1 yards (2nd), while the Jaguars give up 5.2 (24th).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 4.9% of dropbacks (5th), and the Jaguars get home on 6.1% (25th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Dolphins.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: On a typical play the Jaguars gain 4.9 yards (20th), while the Dolphins give up 4.9 (11th).
So the Dolphins have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 61% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Dolphins win about 61 of them. That means the Jaguars win 39, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Dolphins by 3.5, about 62%. I'm at 61%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: This is the part working against my pick: injuries pull my number about 0.7 points toward the Jaguars.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jaguars win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chargers at 55%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Raiders offense ranks 18th, the Chargers defense ranks 13th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Raiders line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (18th), and the Chargers get home on 7.1% (13th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chargers.

other_side.title: When the Chargers have the ball
body: The Chargers score 20.4 points a game (21st in the league), and the Raiders allow 19.5 (7th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Raiders, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: LV have been playing better lately.
items.text: LV are 2-1 over their last three games; LAC are 0-3. They also have about 9 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Raiders are 7th in points allowed per game (19.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Raiders score 14 or more in the first half, the Chargers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 55% actually means

line.body: The line has the Chargers by 3, about 58%. I'm at 55%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 1.0 points further toward the Chargers. The Chargers are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Raiders win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 76%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bengals offense ranks 23rd, the Chiefs defense ranks 1st. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? KC are 3-0 over their last three games; CIN are 1-2. They also have about 5 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, KC are at home.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bengals line gives up a sack on 7.2% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Chiefs get home on 8.3% (1st).
The Bengals score 21.5 points a game (16th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 17.0 (2nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 5.4 yards (6th), while the Bengals give up 5.8 (32nd).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 3.7% of dropbacks (2nd), and the Bengals get home on 6.9% (14th).
So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Bengals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bengals score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Bengals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 76% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 76 of them. That means the Bengals win 24, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 6.5, about 71%. I'm higher at 76%. Most of the gap comes from momentum.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 1.4 points further toward the Chiefs. The Chiefs are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Bengals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Ravens at 79%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Raiders offense ranks 25th, the Ravens defense ranks 1st. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? The game is at M&T Bank Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, BAL have the better scoring margin.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Raiders gain 4.7 yards (25th), while the Ravens give up 4.3 (1st).
The Raiders score 19.5 points a game (23rd in the league), and the Ravens allow 16.2 (1st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Ravens.

other_side.title: When the Ravens have the ball
body: On a typical play the Ravens gain 5.5 yards (4th), while the Raiders give up 5.0 (16th).
The Ravens line gives up a sack on 7.2% of dropbacks (24th), and the Raiders get home on 6.9% (15th).
So the Ravens have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Raiders are 7th in points allowed per game (19.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Raiders score 14 or more in the first half, the Ravens defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 79% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Ravens win about 79 of them. That means the Raiders win 21, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Ravens by 9, about 79%. I'm at 79%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Raiders win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Patriots score 14 or more in the first half, the Seahawks defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 73%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Lions offense ranks 3rd, the Buccaneers defense ranks 19th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Ford Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, rest and weather are about even.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.8 yards (3rd), while the Buccaneers give up 5.1 (19th).

other_side.title: When the Buccaneers have the ball
body: On a typical play the Buccaneers gain 5.0 yards (14th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (26th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Buccaneers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Buccaneers are 5th in points allowed per game (19.2). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Buccaneers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

line.body: The line has the Lions by 7.5, about 76%. I'm at 73%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 0.5 points further toward the Lions. The Lions are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Lucas Oil Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, IND are the healthier team this week.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Colts line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (11th), and the Bears get home on 4.2% (32nd).
The Colts score 23.3 points a game (11th in the league), and the Bears allow 22.3 (19th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Colts.

other_side.title: When the Bears have the ball

The Bears score 21.2 points a game (19th in the league), and the Colts allow 24.4 (28th).
So the Colts have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: CHI have been playing better lately.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Colts have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.

line.body: The line has the Colts by 1.5, about 53%. I'm at 57%, so we basically agree on this one.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 59%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Lions offense ranks 3rd, the Cardinals defense ranks 30th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? Over the last three games, DET and ARI have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.
On top of that, DET have the better scoring margin.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Lions gain 5.8 yards (3rd), while the Cardinals give up 5.6 (30th).
The Lions score 27.4 points a game (5th in the league), and the Cardinals allow 26.8 (31st).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Lions.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 4.7 yards (24th), while the Lions give up 5.4 (26th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Cardinals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Lions have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 59% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Lions win about 59 of them. That means the Cardinals win 41, which is a lot.

line.body: The line has the Lions by 3, about 57%. I'm at 59%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: This is the part working against my pick: injuries pull my number about 1.3 points toward the Cardinals.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Cardinals win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 70%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bills offense ranks 1st, the Jaguars defense ranks 25th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 2-1 over their last three games; JAX are 0-3. They also have about 13 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, BUF are at home.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 3.5% of dropbacks (1st), and the Jaguars get home on 6.1% (25th).
On a typical play the Bills gain 5.5 yards (5th), while the Jaguars give up 5.2 (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: The Jaguars score 22.2 points a game (15th in the league), and the Bills allow 18.7 (3rd).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: JAX's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but JAX have pressured the quarterback on 3% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Allen and stalls drives.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 70% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 70 of them. That means the Jaguars win 30, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Bills by 4, about 66%. I'm at 70%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Jaguars win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Steelers at 58%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Chargers offense ranks 21st, the Steelers defense ranks 8th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.

On top of that, rest and weather are about even.

body: The Chargers score 20.4 points a game (21st in the league), and the Steelers allow 19.7 (8th).

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

line.body: The line has the Steelers by 3, about 57%. I'm at 58%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Chargers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Browns at 68%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Giants offense ranks 32nd, the Browns defense ranks 3rd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Huntington Bank Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, CLE have the better scoring margin.
Quick note: the stats below are from last season (2023), because teams haven't played enough games yet this year to rank them fairly.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Giants line gives up a sack on 12.4% of dropbacks (32nd), and the Browns get home on 8.0% (3rd).
On a typical play the Giants gain 4.3 yards (30th), while the Browns give up 4.3 (3rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Browns.

other_side.title: When the Browns have the ball
body: The Browns score 22.8 points a game (12th in the league), and the Giants allow 23.9 (26th).
The Browns line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (17th), and the Giants get home on 4.9% (31st).
So the Browns have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: NYG's defense has been tougher.
items.text: NYG have allowed noticeably less on a typical play than CLE over the last three games, giving up 20 points a game to CLE's 30. NYG have pressured the quarterback on 30% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for J.Winston to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Giants would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Giants score 14 or more in the first half, the Browns defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 68% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Browns win about 68 of them. That means the Giants win 32, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Browns by 6.5, about 70%. I'm at 68%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Giants win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Packers at 51%, even though the matchups are closer than that sounds.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Vikings offense ranks 3rd, the Packers defense ranks 22nd. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Lambeau Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, gB's pass rush is the difference.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Vikings gain 5.9 yards (3rd), while the Packers give up 5.2 (22nd).
The Vikings line gives up a sack on 9.7% of dropbacks (26th), and the Packers get home on 8.7% (10th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Vikings, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

body: The Packers line gives up a sack on 5.8% of dropbacks (12th), and the Vikings get home on 11.2% (4th).

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Lions at 63%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.

intro: There's a clear lean here, even if it isn't a blowout on paper.
The biggest football reason? The game is at Ford Field. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, DET are the healthier team this week.

body: The Seahawks line gives up a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks (17th), and the Lions get home on 8.4% (12th).

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

body: The Bills score 30.5 points a game (2nd in the league), and the Texans allow 23.5 (22nd).

body: The Texans score 19.8 points a game (17th in the league), and the Bills allow 20.8 (12th).

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Texans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

body: The Jets score 19.0 points a game (21st in the league), and the Vikings allow 14.8 (4th).

That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Vikings.

other_side.title: When the Vikings have the ball
body: The Vikings line gives up a sack on 8.8% of dropbacks (24th), and the Jets get home on 10.1% (4th).

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Jets score 14 or more in the first half, the Vikings defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Jets win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Texans line gives up a sack on 7.4% of dropbacks (22nd), and the Jets get home on 8.3% (5th).

I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Texans, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Eagles offense ranks 10th, the Jaguars defense ranks 29th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? PHI are 3-0 over their last three games; JAX are 1-2. They also have about 18 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, PHI are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Eagles score 24.4 points a game (10th in the league), and the Jaguars allow 28.0 (29th).
On a typical play the Eagles gain 5.5 yards (9th), while the Jaguars give up 5.5 (27th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Eagles.

other_side.title: When the Jaguars have the ball
body: The Jaguars score 21.5 points a game (21st in the league), and the Eagles allow 18.9 (7th).
So the Eagles have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: JAX's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but JAX have pressured the quarterback on 11% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts J.Hurts and stalls drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Jaguars are 10th in yards per play (5.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Jaguars would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Eagles have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Jaguars win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Commanders at 72%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Points per game: the Giants offense ranks 31st, the Commanders defense ranks 10th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? WAS are 2-1 over their last three games; NYG are 0-3. They also have about 24 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, division game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Giants score 14.6 points a game (31st in the league), and the Commanders allow 20.9 (10th).
The Giants line gives up a sack on 7.9% of dropbacks (23rd), and the Commanders get home on 8.6% (4th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Commanders.

other_side.title: When the Commanders have the ball
body: On a typical play the Commanders gain 5.9 yards (4th), while the Giants give up 5.3 (24th).
The Commanders line gives up a sack on 6.1% of dropbacks (15th), and the Giants get home on 12.1% (1st).
So the Commanders have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Giants would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Giants score 14 or more in the first half, the Commanders defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 72% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Commanders win about 72 of them. That means the Giants win 28, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Commanders by 4.5, about 66%. I'm higher at 72%. Most of the gap comes from momentum.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Giants win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Bills at 70%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Bills offense ranks 1st, the Colts defense ranks 26th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? BUF are 3-0 over their last three games; IND are 1-2. They also have about 18 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Bills line gives up a sack on 3.6% of dropbacks (1st), and the Colts get home on 5.4% (26th).
On a typical play the Bills gain 5.4 yards (11th), while the Colts give up 5.4 (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Bills.

other_side.title: When the Colts have the ball
body: The Colts score 20.9 points a game (22nd in the league), and the Bills allow 19.2 (8th).
The Colts line gives up a sack on 5.9% of dropbacks (12th), and the Bills get home on 5.9% (23rd).
So the Bills have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Colts are 12th in points allowed per game (21.4). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Colts would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Bills have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Colts win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 70% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Bills win about 70 of them. That means the Colts win 30, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Bills by 4.5, about 67%. I'm at 70%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Colts win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 82%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Chiefs offense ranks 9th, the Panthers defense ranks 31st. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? Both teams are 2-1 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: KC have about 3 more points of scoring margin per game.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 5.7% of dropbacks (9th), and the Panthers get home on 3.4% (31st).
The Chiefs score 24.0 points a game (11th in the league), and the Panthers allow 31.0 (32nd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Panthers have the ball
body: The Panthers score 16.7 points a game (29th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 19.1 (8th).
On a typical play the Panthers gain 4.5 yards (25th), while the Chiefs give up 4.7 (5th).
So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: CAR's defense has been tougher.
items.text: CAR have allowed noticeably less on a typical play than KC over the last three games, giving up 22 points a game to KC's 23. CAR have pressured the quarterback on 17% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for P.Mahomes to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Panthers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Chiefs have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Panthers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 82% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 82 of them. That means the Panthers win 18, so an upset would be a real surprise.

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 11, about 84%. I'm at 82%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 0.5 points further toward the Chiefs. The Chiefs are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Panthers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 87%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Raiders offense ranks 29th, the Chiefs defense ranks 5th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I don't say this often, but I feel good about this one.
The biggest football reason? KC are 2-1 over their last three games; LV are 0-3. They also have about 13 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, KC are at home.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Raiders gain 4.4 yards (29th), while the Chiefs give up 4.7 (5th).
The Raiders score 18.7 points a game (26th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 19.8 (9th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: The Chiefs score 24.5 points a game (10th in the league), and the Raiders allow 28.5 (29th).
The Chiefs line gives up a sack on 6.1% of dropbacks (14th), and the Raiders get home on 5.2% (27th).
So the Chiefs have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Raiders are 12th in yards per play allowed (5.0). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Raiders score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 87% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 87 of them. That means the Raiders win 13, so an upset would be a real surprise.

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 13.5, about 85%. I'm at 87%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Raiders win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.

If the Giants win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Jets at 52%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Seahawks offense ranks 22nd, the Jets defense ranks 5th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.
The biggest football reason? The game is at MetLife Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, rest tilts toward NYJ.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Seahawks line gives up a sack on 8.0% of dropbacks (22nd), and the Jets get home on 8.6% (5th).
On a typical play the Seahawks gain 5.0 yards (18th), while the Jets give up 4.5 (3rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Jets.

other_side.title: When the Jets have the ball
body: The Jets score 18.5 points a game (27th in the league), and the Seahawks allow 22.2 (14th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Seahawks, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: The offenses have been about even.
items.text: Over the last three games, SEA and NYJ have gained about the same on a typical play, so offense isn't where this game gets decided.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Seahawks would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Seahawks score 14 or more in the first half, the Jets defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Seahawks win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Falcons at 73%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.

intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? Both teams are 0-3 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: ATL have about 10 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, the offenses have been about even.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Falcons line gives up a sack on 5.5% of dropbacks (10th), and the Raiders get home on 6.0% (24th).
The Falcons score 21.4 points a game (19th in the league), and the Raiders allow 27.8 (30th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Falcons.

other_side.title: When the Raiders have the ball
body: The Raiders line gives up a sack on 8.1% of dropbacks (24th), and the Falcons get home on 4.3% (32nd).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Raiders, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Raiders would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Falcons have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Raiders win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

The 49ers score 23.7 points a game (11th in the league), and the Rams allow 25.5 (24th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the Rams have the ball
body: The Rams line gives up a sack on 5.9% of dropbacks (13th), and the 49ers get home on 7.9% (4th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: LA's pass rush is the difference.
items.text: The two defenses have allowed about the same per play, but LA have pressured the quarterback on 9% of dropbacks. Pressure like that disrupts B.Purdy and stalls drives.

items.lead: LA have been playing better lately.
items.text: LA are 2-1 over their last three games; SF are 1-2. They also have about 7 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Rams would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the 49ers have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Rams win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

intro: Okay, this one's close. I went back and forth on it.

The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, LAC are the healthier team this week.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Buccaneers line gives up a sack on 6.8% of dropbacks (19th), and the Chargers get home on 7.5% (12th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chargers.

other_side.title: When the Chargers have the ball
body: The Chargers line gives up a sack on 8.8% of dropbacks (27th), and the Buccaneers get home on 6.5% (18th).
On a typical play the Chargers gain 5.0 yards (16th), while the Buccaneers give up 5.4 (24th).
So the Chargers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: TB have been playing better lately.
items.text: TB are 3-0 over their last three games; LAC are 1-2. They also have about 15 more points of scoring margin per game.

items.lead: TB's defense has been tougher.
items.text: TB have allowed much less on a typical play than LAC over the last three games, giving up 14 points a game to LAC's 21. TB have pressured the quarterback on 24% of dropbacks. That makes it harder for J.Herbert to put together scoring drives.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Buccaneers are 5th in points per game (27.9). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

change_my_mind: If the Buccaneers score 14 or more in the first half, the Chargers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Buccaneers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the 49ers at 57%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Dolphins offense ranks 24th, the 49ers defense ranks 10th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: Honestly? This is close to a coin flip, and I want to show you why.
The biggest football reason? Both teams are 1-2 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: SF have about 3 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, SF are the healthier team this week.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Dolphins gain 4.7 yards (24th), while the 49ers give up 4.9 (10th).
The Dolphins line gives up a sack on 6.5% of dropbacks (18th), and the 49ers get home on 7.4% (10th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the 49ers.

other_side.title: When the 49ers have the ball
body: The 49ers line gives up a sack on 6.0% of dropbacks (14th), and the Dolphins get home on 5.4% (27th).
So the 49ers have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: MIA's offense is heating up.
items.text: Over the last three games, MIA have gained noticeably more on a typical play than SF, scoring 20 points a game to SF's 18. Expect MIA to move the ball more consistently.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Dolphins are 12th in yards per play allowed (4.9). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.

change_my_mind: If the Dolphins score 14 or more in the first half, the 49ers defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Dolphins win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Rams at 74%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their offense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Rams offense ranks 13th, the Cardinals defense ranks 25th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? The game is at SoFi Stadium. Before any matchup data, playing at home is worth about 5.9 points of win chance in my model.
On top of that, LA have been playing better lately.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Rams gain 5.2 yards (13th), while the Cardinals give up 5.3 (25th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Rams.

other_side.title: When the Cardinals have the ball
body: On a typical play the Cardinals gain 5.5 yards (7th), while the Rams give up 5.3 (21st).
The Cardinals line gives up a sack on 5.2% of dropbacks (7th), and the Rams get home on 6.2% (20th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Cardinals, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Cardinals are 7th in yards per play (5.5). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Cardinals would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Rams have fewer than 10 points at halftime, the matchup I'm counting on isn't happening, and I'd call it a coin flip.
If the Cardinals win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

primary_reason: Sportsbooks have BAL as a 5.5-point favorite, which works out to about a 68% chance to win. Clark also picks BAL.
secondary_reason: Both teams are 2-1 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: BAL have about 10 more points of scoring margin per game.
risk_factor: HOU have home field, worth about 5.9 points of win chance.
flip_scenarios: If BAL loses turnover margin by 2+, its win probability can collapse quickly.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Ravens at 70%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Sack rate: the Texans offense ranks 26th, the Ravens defense ranks 6th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: This is one of my more confident calls of the week.
The biggest football reason? Both teams are 2-1 over their last three, so the records are even. The difference is scoring margin: BAL have about 10 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, bAL's offense has been more productive.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: The Texans line gives up a sack on 8.2% of dropbacks (26th), and the Ravens get home on 7.6% (6th).
On a typical play the Texans gain 4.8 yards (23rd), while the Ravens give up 4.9 (9th).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Ravens.

other_side.title: When the Ravens have the ball
body: The Ravens score 30.1 points a game (3rd in the league), and the Texans allow 21.8 (9th).
So the Ravens have the better of this side too, which is part of why I'm comfortable.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Texans are 4th in yards per play allowed (4.7). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Texans would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Texans score 14 or more in the first half, the Ravens defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Texans win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 70% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Ravens win about 70 of them. That means the Texans win 30, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Ravens by 5.5, about 68%. I'm at 70%, so we basically agree on this one.

injuries.title: Injuries I'm factoring in
injuries.body: Both teams have guys on the injury report, but it roughly evens out, so it barely moves my number.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Texans win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.

clark_report.headline: I'm on the Chiefs at 66%, and the biggest mismatch on the field is their defense.
clark_report.dek: Yards per play: the Steelers offense ranks 21st, the Chiefs defense ranks 6th. That's the biggest mismatch on the field.
intro: I like this pick, but it's not a runaway.
The biggest football reason? KC are 3-0 over their last three games; PIT are 1-2. They also have about 14 more points of scoring margin per game.
On top of that, KC are the healthier team this week.

deciding.title: The matchup that decides it
body: On a typical play the Steelers gain 4.8 yards (21st), while the Chiefs give up 4.8 (6th).
The Steelers score 23.5 points a game (12th in the league), and the Chiefs allow 18.5 (3rd).
That's the number that jumped out at me: it's the biggest mismatch on the field, and it favors the Chiefs.

other_side.title: When the Chiefs have the ball
body: On a typical play the Chiefs gain 4.9 yards (18th), while the Steelers give up 4.9 (10th).
I'll be honest: this side of the ball favors the Steelers, and it's the part that keeps my number from going higher.

items.lead: Lean on what they do best.
items.text: The Steelers are 7th in points allowed per game (19.9). If that shows up, this gets tight fast.

items.lead: Win the turnover battle.
items.text: Two extra possessions for the Steelers would erase most of the edge I just described.

change_my_mind: If the Steelers score 14 or more in the first half, the Chiefs defense isn't doing what I expected, and I'd lean their way.
If the Steelers win the turnover battle by 2 or more, I'd make them the favorite.
If either starting quarterback is ruled out before kickoff, ignore this report and check back.

meaning.title: What 66% actually means
meaning.body: If this game were played 100 times, I think the Chiefs win about 66 of them. That means the Steelers win 34, which is not nothing.

line.body: The line has the Chiefs by 3, about 59%. I'm higher at 66%. Most of the gap comes from momentum.

injuries.body: The injury report pushes me about 0.7 points further toward the Chiefs. The Chiefs are the healthier team this week.

clark_report.signoff: Not a lock! If the Steelers win the turnover battle, I'm probably wrong, and you'll hear about it in the recap.
